articles.title: 'Survivor 51' Star Kristin Flickinger on Her Chaotic Exit, Being an Unexpected Threat and Overwhelming Fan Response
articles.summary: After 26 years of trying to get on the show, the longtime superfan explains why she'd happily wait another 26 to do it all again.
articles.content:
Kristin Flickinger waited 26 years to play Survivor , and when she finally got her chance, she proved that all those years of preparation weren't for nothing. From her impressive survival skills to navigating the game with a broken foot, Kristin quickly established herself as one of Survivor 51's most memorable castaways. But despite spending decades studying the game, there was one thing she never anticipated: being considered a social threat. That reputation, combined with a chaotic Tribal Council featuring multiple twists and advantages, ultimately brought her long-awaited adventure to an end. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Cupertino' Moving, 'Ghosts' Doubling Up on CBS' Midseason Schedule TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners

In an exclusive interview with The Hollywood Reporter , Kristin opens up about her elimination, why pairing with Kilby was a strategic misstep and the overwhelmingly positive response she's received from fans. She also reflects on her decades-long pursuit of a spot on the show and shares a hilarious behind-the-scenes story involving a boat, a broken foot and a whole lot of waving.

At one point at Tribal Council you ask, “Is anyone playing the game they thought they were gonna play?” which I found interesting. Where or when did your game take a detour from your plans?

I studied for a long time and I studied with the thinking that I'll just get all of this knowledge, and then I can kind of toss away any plans and be fluid and pull on all of the different parts of my understanding of the game. And I did that. I went out with a half a vote with four intersecting, interlocking wild twists. So I feel good about that. But I think what I was referring to then was that I thought I would come in and be this huge thinky presence, which in some ways I was. I didn't think I would be a social threat. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Even now, I can't even say it. A social threat is not what I thought was going to happen. So when people were like, “You're just too liked,” I don't know what to do with that, man. All I'm doing is showing up and being myself and doing too much. And people saw me as a social threat. So it was confusing to me and I didn't know how to get out of that because I had never planned for that. It's permanent uncertainty. I think a lot of folks went in thinking they were going to play a certain way and it's very hard to do when you don't know what's coming. For me, I begged for this. I wanted to be on 51 because I thought a lot of people are going to think something new is happening, but they won't know what the new is.

Then I can tell them what the new is and I can convince them of it and I'll have a strategic advantage. And then it was even better than that because it was the theme of the season. But everybody out there was thinking like me. Everybody came to play. Everyone understood the assignment. This cast is fire. It is just nonstop from start to finish, nonstop.

You went home because of a single vote: Devin's. Does that make the loss easier to accept because you had a good read on where everyone stood, or harder because your fate came down to one person's decision?

Half a vote. I think for some folks it might be harder. For me, this was an iconic vote out. It was an epic Tribal Council. It was Adventageddon 2.0. Does it make it easy to go out? I'm not sure anyone would be like, “Yeah, that was easy.” No, I think it's hard to go out and after 26 years, really hard to go out. At the same time, I had been segregated from everyone. I was the only person that went to Tribal Council once pre-merge. People were building by attrition. I had to build by addition. So people were going and voting folks out and they were coming back together and understanding where they were. I didn't have that. I had to be working with everyone. I had to try to work with Maggie. I had a long conversation with Dev. I had a long conversation with Lewis. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I had long conversations that day with people I'd never talked to. So to see for me that that paid off and I had this one vote that was smart to play. They split the vote. That's a smart thing to do. They thought I had something. Okay, I didn't have something, but I knew that I needed to play my shot in the dark. I understood that intuitively. You play your best. Luck happens in Survivor . I've studied this game a long time. I know luck is a part of it, so luck comes into play, that's fair.

Let's go back to when you guys learned about the duo twist. How did you know what it was and walk me through the process of how you ended up with Kilby and why not immediately pair up with Sharonda because of the tethered idol?

We knew what it was because we were made aware of a couple of the twists in the season. We were made aware of what Double Duos was. We were made aware of Coin Flip. So we knew that those things had played in 50. You'll hear me in my confessional say, “It's either we're playing together or we're going to compete against each other.” That was because also I watched Drag Race and I know from year to year, they'll swap it around. So I was like, I don't know which one this is, girl. Let's get ready.

In terms of getting paired up with Kilby, at that point I knew that my threat level was skyrocketing. People thought I had not one idol, but multiple idols. I tried to turn that down my threat level when I came back from Exile and I told them that I had gotten a build your own fake immunity idol kit. I told them that I made an idol out of beads I'd stolen from the Savu flag when I was laid up with a broken foot in camp. I brought it back, I told them, I put it down in camp and they said, “Don't touch it. It's probably a cursed idol.” So my threat level, no matter what I did, was just increasing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But why not pair up with Sharonda instead of Kilby? At that point I put my hand up and I said, “Hey guys, I know that I'm not great physically right now with my broken foot. If anyone wants to pair up with me, that would be so nice. I'm still good at puzzles.” And Kilby raised his hand and said, “I'll pair up with you, Kristin.” And it was like, “Oh no,” because Kilby was not at the top of anyone's list, but he was absolutely a threat. He was a strategic threat. He was a social threat, and he had pissed some people off. The two of us together I knew was a problem. We were just too plum a target. You couldn't have pretended you didn't hear him and then just started walking away? I was in the hammock with Jelly when this all went down and I was like, “Okay, Kilbs, let's see whoever anybody else wants to pair up with.” And then I turned to Jelly and Devin was like, “I'll take Jelly.” And I was trying to get Sharonda's eye, strategically. I very rarely did anything that wasn't very strategic. This one just didn't pay off.

Of all the players this season, you were the most prepared. You knew how to make a fire, what to eat, and seemed at ease on the island. Is that why players saw you as a “white whale” or was it something else they were picking up on?

I mean, you'd have to ask them. I studied my butt off, and this is also just me. I went out there, I tried to not do so much. There were times when I kind of pulled back a little bit, but I wanted to provide for people because I wanted to keep us strong, especially in the tribe portion of the game. I wanted us to be strong so we could compete. But it's hard to say, I don't know.

My partner was like, “You are going to walk in and they're going see you as a threat.” And honestly, that's my life. This is nothing new. People see me as a threat when I walk in the room. That's okay. Over time, I figured out how to deal with that. There are times when people are just like, “That person's too much of a threat.” I walked away thinking I will never again try to manage people's concern about whether I'm a threat. My threat level, I really don't care what people think about it in life. I could have played always as a threat and said, “I've got four idols come at me.” And it wouldn't have changed anything in terms of how people perceived me.

I'm pretty certain you're the first player to get a montage of applying for Survivor for 20+ years. You didn't get the title of Sole Survivor but you impacted the game. Was your experience what you were hoping for?

I felt like my playing was a love letter to something that I love deeply. It was a love letter to the game, and it felt like a love letter back with that montage. I have those videos. I have the VHS tapes. I've saved them forever because they're precious to me. This journey is precious to me, and it was precious before I got out there. I had a 25-year survivor journey before I ever played. I learned so much through the application processes. I learned so much thinking about my life in terms of survivor. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Maybe that's really toxic to Survivoriize your whole life. I don't freaking know. But yeah, it was worth it. It was incredible. I would wait another 26 years. I really, hope I don't have to, but it was a beautiful, beautiful experience. I don't take any of it for granted. I'm so unbelievably grateful. And when I came out of the game, honestly, I was euphoric. I was joyful and grateful in a way that I have rarely experienced.

What does it feel like to want to be on the show and applying for so long and for your personality to resonate with so many people?

It's wild. I had a great journey before, and then I got to play the game, which was everything. It was everything. I got to go to Exile Island. I communed with the islands. It was everything. And then I came out and I got to watch it on television, and I know that it's television and you can't show everything, and I thought those two experiences might not match up completely. They matched up a lot, and I also don't take that for granted. I'm so grateful for that. And then to see myself, the way that I experience myself and the way that I experienced myself in the game is a gift that not everyone gets.

Then to have people respond to that positively, I planned for what to do with negative feedback. I planned for how to stay off of social media and not get taken down with it. I did not plan for what it would be like to receive 99.9% positive feedback. So it's overwhelming. It's really overwhelming, honestly. I'm so, so grateful. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Would you like a behind the scenes exclusive?

Okay, for the Summit. This is a funny, this is a silly one, but when I got selected for the Summit, I was so excited. I walked down to the boat to get on and go out, and the boat was out a little ways, so I waded out up to my knees, and I was waving to everybody. I was waiting, I was waving, and I was waiting for the boat to come in. I don't know how long I stood there. I probably said goodbye to everybody and waved five times before I realized I had to walk out to the boat. I looked ridiculous. And then I had to wade far out there, and I had a broken foot, and it's up to my waist. So I went to the back of the boat where it was not moving as much and hoisted myself up. I was like, oh my God. I don't know what I thought. It was just going to come in and scoop me.

articles.title: New PS5 Console Update Released Just Before GTA 6 Launch
articles.summary: PlayStation has today released a new system update for PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles right before the arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. Although GTA 6 isn't a PS5-exclusive, it's undoubtedly going to end up being the most-played game of the year on the platform. As a result, PlayStation has now let loose a new […]
articles.content:
Downloadable now, PS5 firmware version 26.07-14.23.00 is a very small update for the platform. Rather than making any holistic changes to the PS5's UI, dashboard, or other features, the only thing that this patch does is make “security fixes to the system software.” Although it's a bit disappointing to see the update be so small in nature, it's also unsurprising given how many miniature patches of this sort have released throughout the life of the PS5.

More recently, though, this new PS5 system update is the second one that has been released in November that has only been tied to improving the hardware's security. In recent months, PS5 jailbreaking has become much more common, which has allowed users to gain access to the console's entire library of games without having to pay for them. Naturally, PlayStation has been looking to squash making these jailbreaks possible, which has prompted it to release new firmware updates at a faster rate than normal.

As mentioned, with Grand Theft Auto 6 far and away being the biggest release of the year on PS5, PlayStation undoubtedly wants to ensure that the game cannot be easily pirated on jailbroken consoles. Not only would Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive lose out on money if users were able to get ahold of GTA 6 through improper means, but PlayStation would lose a substantial amount itself, as all purchases of the game on the PS Store directly benefit the platform holder. Because of this, the timing of this new PS5 update is surely no accident, as PlayStation wants to make sure it has the best security measures in place.

Looking ahead, this could end up being one of the final PS5 firmware updates released in 2026. Historically, PlayStation tends to do very little with the PS5 during December, as the company tends to go silent around the holidays. If there is a new update released for the PS5 and PS5 Pro in the near future, though, we'll be sure to let you know here on ComicBook .

articles.title: Jon Stewart’s Unexpected Batman Comment After Pattinson Landed Bond Had Me Laughing Out Loud
articles.summary: One iconic movie character per actor and at a time, Pattinson!
articles.content:
Robert Pattinson has had a pretty ridiculous year. Between The Drama , Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey , and the upcoming Dune: Part Three on the 2026 movie schedule , he's been keeping busy. Now, as if playing the Dark Knight wasn't enough, he's officially been cast as the next James Bond . Naturally, the announcement has generated plenty of reactions, but I wasn't expecting Jon Stewart to have one of the funniest takes I've heard so far.

When your flight gets canceled, logic dictates that the next step is to hop aboard a riverboat. Obviously. Unfortunately for Stewart, his backup transportation wasn't particularly reliable either, and things only got worse when he tried to contact the people running the audition. He continued the bit:

I was already laughing at the idea of Stewart missing out on a big role because his riverboat ran into trouble and Microsoft Outlook wasn't cooperating. But he saved his best complaint for last, taking issue with the fact that Pattinson already has another pretty famous character on his résumé. Raising his fist in mock frustration, the longtime late-night host shouted:

I mean, he's got a point. How many iconic characters does one guy need? Here's an actor who has already played Edward Cullen in the Twilight movies, Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter , and Bruce Wayne in The Batman . Now he's adding 007 to the résumé. At this rate, I half expect someone to announce him as the next Superman. Hey, with James Gunn’s recent outing anything is possible.

Of course, Stewart was having fun with the news, and I don't think anybody seriously believes Pattinson should be disqualified from playing Bond because he's already Batman. But I do think it's funny that the actor is becoming the face of another enormous franchise while he's still working on The Batman: Part II .

Robert Pattinson's first James Bond movie doesn't have a release date yet, although production is expected to begin sometime in 2027. Meanwhile, The Batman: Part II is currently scheduled for February 2028.

In tonight's episode titled “Shot Through the Heart," past and present collide for Gibbs (Harmon) as he searches for answers about what happened to Lala (Mariel Molino) all those years ago. David J. North, showrunner and executive producer of NCIS: Origins , teases how Gibbs is able to meet his younger self in the episode.

“Gibbs was shot in the season premiere, and he hasn't had time to tend to his injury properly. He's been a little busy. But the effects of his injury are finally catching up to him, and the mind can play tricks on you when you're injured. In the history of NCIS , we've seen Gibbs go into a dream-like state several times, and it's fun to take a wild trip into his mind,” North shared.

articles.title: David Ayer to Become a Partner at Ryan Kavanaugh’s New Location-Defying AI Company (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The 'Heart of the Beast’ director believes ACME AI's tech makes many location shoots moot: "This pulls so many stories within striking distance.”
articles.content: He may have headed into the rugged with Heart of the Beast , but David Ayer says he may now have a new and more technological solution to shooting in the wilderness: AI . The director is joining ACME AI as a principal and managing partner, and will be involved in the operations of the firm. Founded by former Relativity Media co-founder Ryan Kavanaugh , ACME and its "Grey Box" tech allows directors and actors to shoot full-fledged scenes in far-flung locales without going anywhere. “When I got in there and saw what the tech can do I felt like a cowboy coming in off the range and seeing the first automobile," Ayer tells The Hollywood Reporter . "I thought ‘I better learn how to drive this car or I'm going to be out a of a job.'” The Model T in question is known as performance transfer, and essentially it keeps above-the-line work intact while radically reducing the need for, and expense of, much of the below-the-line kind. ACME is part of a new wave of filmmaker-centric companies — they also include Jon Erwin's Innovative Dreams and Matt Stone and Trey Parker's Deep Voodoo — that allow for actors to perform dynamically in front of real-looking backdrops without ever leaving a soundstage. Romantic shots in the foreground of the Eiffel Tower? Check. Chase scenes through the streets of Tokyo? Why not? Essentially performance transfer functions as a digital green screen, but for everything. Proponents say the technique preserves all the physical aspects of a performance (and actors' jobs) at far lower cost to a studio or the climate; think of it as Zoom work for thespians. Critics, however, say it risks losing the magic and serendipity of physical locations and hurts the livelihoods of on-set workers besides. (Department heads such as production designers and lighting artists would in many cases still be used, but in a more supervisory/advisory way than on a physical set.) Ayer says the chance to bring productions in at a much lower budget and nab greenlights that would otherwise prove out of reach makes it worth the tradeoff. “As a storyteller half my job is litigating over budget," he says. "This pulls so many stories within striking distance." ACME believes that, without the need to pack up and travel to a particular piece of geography and then set up shoots there, its tech can lead to a reduction in time and money at a rate of between 50 and 75 percent. To create the tech, ACME mapped many lenses and lighting packages to allow for a greater photorealism, and combined it with models that allow for the re-creation of the physical world. ACME's Grey Box currently exists in Los Angeles on a dedicated stage, but the system could theoretically be replicated in other locations. (The company will rent the tech out to studios the way many soundstages currently do.) Doug Liman recently completed shooting the origins-of-crypto drama Bitcoin starring Casey Affleck using ACME's Grey Box. The movie explores the mysterious origins of the title currency's pseudonymous founder Satoshi Nakamoto without, for the most part, leaving the stage despite the Australian and other global settings. The idea of making big-budget-looking movies possible at mid-budget prices could, if successful, prompt a host of downstream questions. Will audiences stop valuing (and paying for) high-octane spectacle in the same way given how much easier it will be to produce? Will a whole system of crews and physical locations be displaced? Will studio executives eventually put pressure even on mid-budget projects to lower their costs given the expectation of cheaper methods? And who, besides Christopher Nolan and Tom Cruise, will actually be allowed to shoot in intensive physical locations for months at a time? A former Navy enlistee, Ayer has had an eventful Hollywood trajectory. After an early career writing or directing acclaimed law-and-order-themed dramas ( Training Day , End of Watch) he entered the DCEU with 2016's controversial Suicide Squad (on which he famously had a very different cut ). He has entered a new act with a spate of successes in the past few years, including the Jason Statham action film The Beekeeper and this fall's dog survival thriller Beast s tarring Brad Pitt. It garnered strong reviews and became a solid worldwide hit . Ayer says he has at multiple projects in development that can be redirected to the Grey Box. He believes many entities in the creative ecosystem will benefit from such a re-channeling, including actors and directors. “The staging starts to feel more like a Broadway play, where you know exactly what you're going to get," he says. "If I'm not worried about getting kicked off a location or a lightning storm shutting me down, it takes away a lot of the friction of filmmaking and just lets me focus on the fine craft of directing."

articles.title: Home Alone Sequel Video Brings Back Macaulay Culkin After 34 Years
articles.summary: Macaulay Culkin is back as his Home Alone character, Kevin McCallister, just not in the way anyone expected. It's been thirty-four years since Culkin played the part in 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, and though the series continued without him and his career carried on, the two never intersected again, officially at […]
articles.content:
McDonald's has released a new ad for their upcoming “The Home Alone Meal” that will make its way to the fast food chain starting on December 1st. The perfect way to sell such a meal, which includes Home Alone-themed socks with the various McDonald's characters, is to once again bring back Macaulay Culkin as Kevin McCallister, who not only cheekily references that he's “alone….again” in the ad but then recreates some of the elements from the movie itself all inside a McDonald's restaurant. Watch it for yourself below.

A return of Macaulay Culkin as Kevin McCallister in an ad shouldn't shock fans who are familiar with his work in recent years, but it is surprising given the actor has already made it clear that plans may be in motion for his actual big-screen return. Earlier this summer, word came that Disney is reportedly “salivating” over the potential of Culkin returning to the role for a new Home Alone sequel. Culkin has previously teased his idea for a new movie, noting that it would follow a grown Kevin McCallister, now a single father, who is resented by his son. In the film, according to Culkin's pitch, the youngster would lock him out of the house and then set the traps for him upon reentry.

It's worth noting that the first two Home Alone movies were massive success stories upon release. The first film made over $476 million at the global box office back in 1990 (over $1.2 billion when adjusted for inflation into 2026 dollars), with the sequel making over $358 million globally just two years later. Four more movies were made in the series afterward, though none of the same creatives returned for any of the sequels. If Macaulay Culkin were to return to the series, it would not only give the franchise some juice that it had completely lost, but no doubt give him a career resurgence.

articles.title: Palworld Puts a Brief Pause on New Updates, But the Reason Makes Perfect Sense
articles.summary: Developer Pocketpair is holding back news about Palworld 1.1 and Palfarm because it doesn't want to compete with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. With Rockstar's long-awaited blockbuster arriving this week, the studio apparently recognizes that this isn't the ideal moment to draw attention to anything else. The explanation came directly from John "Bucky" […]
articles.content:
The explanation came directly from John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair's head of communications and publishing, who responded to a fan asking about the lack of news for both projects. As reported by GamesRadar , Buckley explained that sharing announcements during GTA 6's launch week was “probably not the best idea” from a public relations perspective. The statement came in response to an X user, @Raiderknight, who asked Buckley when fans could expect more news about Palworld 1.1 and Palfarm .

Pocketpair is well aware of what is happening this week. In truth, there are exceedingly few games and franchises capable of commanding the kind of attention Grand Theft Auto 6 is about to receive. Rockstar's next open-world blockbuster has spent numerous years building up hype and anticipation for its fans. Come its November 19 launch, it is expected to utterly dominate almost all gaming conversations across social media, news outlets, and streaming platforms. Even major announcements from established franchises could genuinely struggle to make much of an impression while the world is busy exploring GTA 6's reimagining of Vice City.

From Pocketpair's perspective, holding off on news is simply a matter of choosing the right moment to reveal upcoming content. Announcing a substantial Palworld update or revealing more about Palfarm only for the news to disappear beneath a tidal wave of GTA 6 coverage would accomplish very little. The studio could put considerable effort into building excitement, only to find that much of its audience is focused elsewhere. Such is a likely occurrence, which is why Pocketpair had decided to waiting a little longer before announcing anything. The logic is that those announcements stand a better chance of reaching the people they're actually intended for.

Sharing news about Palworld 1.1 or Palfarm the week GTA6 is about to drop is probably not the best idea… 🙂 From a PR point of view!

Importantly, Buckley's comments concern announcements rather than any sort developmental pause. Pocketpair hasn't suggested that work on either project has stopped, nor has it provided a new schedule for when fans can expect more information. The studio is simply choosing not to fight for the spotlight during one of the biggest gaming launches in years. It's a sensible decision, even if fans waiting for updates will have to exercise a little more restraint and wait a little longer.

It's a rare glimpse into the strategic decisions developers have to make when sharing the spotlight with a release as anticipated as GTA 6 . The industry is full of studios trying to make their releases stand out, but sometimes the smartest marketing decision is knowing when not to make an announcement at all. Pocketpair has apparently decided that going up against Rockstar this week would be a losing battle, and it's hard to blame the studio for that. In fact, most would likely agree that this is the best decision for scenario.

"I started reading it, and I got through about 10 pages," he said. "When [the FBI agent] Crawford said, ‘You don't want Hannibal Lecter inside your head,' I thought, ‘Ooh, that's it.' EXCLUSIVE: Award-winning writer, director and producer Georgia Lee has signed on as showrunner of Zhong Kui: Demon Slayer (working title), a supernatural drama series about one of Chinese culture's most powerful mythological figures.

Lee is a co-executive producer on HBO's recently announced Crazy Rich Asians television series, and previously served as showrunner and executive producer of Netflix's Partner Track . She was also a writer and co-producer on the acclaimed sci-fi space opera The Expanse .

Singapore-based production house Matlock Stone has developed the project in partnership with Janet Yang Productions, founded by the producer and former AMPAS president, and Sunny View Media. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Books Kristen Ciccarelli's 'Crimson Moth' Book Series In Development For TV Adaptation With 'The 100's Kim Shumway Penning Script News Co-production More Important Than Ever In AI Era, Say Filmart Panelists: "Those Days Of The Blockbusters Are Gone"

Lee and Yang will both executive produce the series, along with Hong Kong actor Simon Yam; Emmy-nominated editor Zimo Huang; Sean Ng; and Jin Li Lim. According to Chinese legend, Zhong Kui was a brilliant scholar in Tang Dynasty China who took his own life after being unjustly denied an imperial appointment. Recognised after death for his integrity and fierce sense of justice, he was elevated to become the King of Ghosts, taking his place in the Chinese pantheon as a powerful demon-slayer and protector of the mortal world from supernatural evil.

Like other Chinese mythological figures including Nezha and Sun Wukong (a.k.a. the Monkey King), Zhong Kui features regularly in Chinese, Korean and Japanese pop culture across film, television, comics and video games. These include Tencent's hugely popular mobile game Honor Of Kings and Game Science's upcoming Black Myth: Zhong Kui , the follow-up to the wildly successful Black Myth: Wukong game.

Set in contemporary Hong Kong, Zhong Kui: Demon Slayer brings the legendary figure into the modern world after a century-long absence. Disillusioned after more than a thousand years of protecting humanity, Zhong Kui is reluctantly drawn back into action, confronting a world transformed in his absence – and an evil that has evolved with it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Lee's credits also include 2005 indie film Red Doors , which she wrote and directed. She started her career apprenticing on Gangs Of New Yor k after its director Martin Scorsese saw her first short film, The Big Dish .

Commenting on Zhong Kui: Demon Slayer , Lee said: "Zhong Kui is one of the great figures of Chinese mythology, and I'm thrilled to bring him to life. I've long been drawn to stories about the struggle between hope and despair, and Zhong Kui lets us explore that eternal conflict on two scales at once: the intensely personal journey of one man, and the larger battle for humanity's soul.

"I've always believed the most specific stories, rooted deeply in a particular culture and point of view, are the ones that speak most universally. I'm excited to share the richness of Chinese folklore with a global audience through a story about the power of forgiveness, hope, and grace in the face of cynicism and despair."

Yang added: "Ever since meeting her over 20 years ago, Georgia has always impressed me with her brilliant, curious mind, and passion for storytelling. She is particularly fond of comic books (having even published her own) and sci-fi, having gotten her start in TV writing on the iconic show The Expanse . Add to this her deep exploration of Asian-American identity and early mentorship under Martin Scorsese, she undoubtedly brings a unique perspective to this project.

"With the rise of K-pop and Asian dramas, to the success of games like Black Myth: Wukong , and even internet trends like Chinamaxxing, we're witnessing a growing global fascination with Asian culture. With Zhong Kui , we have a highly-beloved character from the rich world of Chinese mythology, but we place him in a contemporary setting, ensuring he will be equally embraced by those meeting him for the first time."

Yam, one of Hong Kong's most iconic actors, said: "Chinese culture has thousands of years of rich stories, traditions and extraordinary figures that have so much to offer audiences today. These stories have travelled far and wide over the millennia, and today there is a real appetite to discover so much more.

"Zhong Kui is one of the great figures from that profound heritage, but what makes him exciting to me is how much there is to explore. He comes from another time, yet so much of what surrounds him – how we think about justice, human nature, the choices people make and the world we create for ourselves – feels just as relevant today."

Zhong Kui: Demon Slayer i s currently in development. Zimo Huang is represented by Brian Goldberg of Ascent. Georgia Lee is represented by Lee Rosenbaum of RLG LLP, and Abby Glusker and Mickey Berman of UTA. Matlock Stone is represented by Chace McGuire of Myman Greenspan.

articles.title: Black Clover Season 2 Gives Noelle the Reunion She's Been Waiting 9 Years For
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Pierrot Black Clover Season 2 has been giving its characters some big moments that fans have been waiting for since the anime began nearly a decade ago, and the newest episode gave Noelle's family a much needed reunion after her big win. Black Clover Season 2 is now in the midst of the Spade Kingdom Raid […]
articles.content:
Black Clover Season 2 has ramped up the fight against Megicula as while Noelle was able to reach the supremely strong Saint Stage for a short time , it was still not enough to deal the final blow to the Supreme Devil before it was too late. Luckily, her brother Nozel arrived just in time to help her and Noelle was able to fully defeat Megicula with the help of the others. Resulting in the brief return of their mother Acier as she praises them for making it this far.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 7 sees Nozel arriving to help Noelle just in time, and through a flashback it's explained why he's been so distant from her all this time. Acier had previously fought against Vanica when Megicula first formed a contract with her, and it left the Silva mother with a curse that slowly killed her from the inside out. Nozel had seen it all go down, but he was also cursed in that moment to keep Acier's real cause of death a secret or he would die as well.

Nozel took on the brunt of his pain alone, and thus had pushed Noelle away by treating her so harshly while he sought out power to take down Megicula in his own way. But with the Supreme Devil's defeat with the latest episode, Acier's spirit briefly appears before the two siblings and praises them for how hard they have worked for all this time. It's an emotional full circle moment for this family that has been so broken apart after the matriarch's death, and hopefully opens up a path forward.

Black Clover Season 2 has had some big developments for Noelle as not only has she gotten physically stronger, she's also made some big emotional changes as well. This moment with her brother is likely to strengthen their connection with one another and hopefully begins the path to healing from their strained history, but Noelle has also become much more self-realized. This same fight also saw Noelle fully accept that she has romantic feelings for Asta , and she's no longer hiding from that fact.

But fans of Yuki Tabata's original Black Clover manga series know that this is unfortunately far from the end of everything. This is all leading to a much bigger arc to come with even more intense fights for Noelle and the others, so it just remains to be seen how the anime is going to tackle everything from here on out . How do you feel about all of Noelle's big moments in Black Clover ‘s latest episode? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

The new meal, which includes side items inspired by things Kevin McAllister likes and socks with designs featuring McDonald's characters like Grimace and Birdie, will be made available on December 1.

The actor has revived what is arguably one of his most famous roles before. In 2018, he played Kevin in a spot for Google Assistant, using the device to do everything from order food to keep track on who might ring the doorbell.

Trying to harness the power of popular film is a go-to technique for many big advertisers. Both General Motors and Verizon, for example, have convened the cast of 1997's “Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery” for big-budget ads, asking actor and creator Mike Myers to create new scenarios for its characters. GM used the cast in a Super Bowl commercial in 2022 to out what was then a growing fleet of electric vehicles. Verizon used the movie's characters this year to talk up a new subscriber plan that includes perks and rewards.

Even Hollywood's most beloved figures might make a return for commercial purposes. Comcast in 2019 ran a longform commercial during NBC's telecast of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade featuring E.T., the alien creature of the same name from the 1982 movie. articles.title: Florence Pugh Wants James Bond Role Alongside Robert Pattinson, But Not as the Bond Girl
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson was announced as the new James Bond yesterday, and now, MCU favorite and Pattinson's Dune co-star Florence Pugh wants in on the reboot of the franchise too—just not in the role that many are expecting. For months, there was intense speculation regarding who might be stepping into this iconic role, with names like […]
articles.content:
Now, that's been confirmed, along with a first look at Pattinson as Bond that has fans more than a little excited for the movie to come (which isn't expected until about late 2028). While the other casting decisions and the story beats aren't currently known, and it will likely be quite some time before any of those details start coming through, Florence Pugh is taking this opportunity to pitch her potential role in the upcoming Bond film, and it's actually perfect. Check out her exact comments during Elle's Women in Hollywood 2026 event below.

Speaking during Elle's Women in Hollywood 2026 event, Pugh revealed that she had sent director of the upcoming James Bond movie Denis Villeneuve a text about wanting a villain role in the film, explaining, “I said, ‘Congratulations on finding your Bond. Nice catch. Any villains with the size of 5'4″ female?'” Although this moment of Pugh's speech certainly got a laugh, and she's known for plenty of similar funny moments, she seemed quite serious in her interest, and it would actually be the perfect role for her. Sure, some might expect Pugh to step into the world of James Bond as a “Bond girl,” but MCU fans know that she would be beyond brilliant as a villain in the franchise.

florence pugh told denis villeneuve she would be up to play the villain in his james bond film pic.twitter.com/H3CP1zDShP

Among her many other titles over the last several years, Pugh has become a major aspect of the MCU franchise. Following her debut in Black Widow as Natasha's sort of little sister Yelena, her character returned in Hawkeye and then played a huge role in Thunderbolts* . Yelena has since appeared in Spider-Man: Brand New Day as well, cementing that the “New Avengers” of Thunderbolts* will be a serious component of the MCU moving forward, and that's only being reinforced by what seems to be Pugh's very important role in Avengers: Doomsday , which is just one month away.

There are certainly other roles in which Pugh has proven her acting chops, and Yelena isn't a villain (although it seemed touch and go at the start of Black Widow ), but her appearances as Yelena have more than cemented that she would be perfect for a villain in the new James Bond movie. Now, it's just a waiting game to see whether this will truly come to pass.

Would you want to see Pugh as a Bond villain? Let us know in the comments down below.

Rosalía, who is nominated for nine awards at the 2027 Grammys, will receive the Hitmakers Masterpiece of the Decade honor for her groundbreaking album "LUX," Hilary Duff will receive the Generational Icon Award, and Slayyyter will receive the Breakthrough Artist of the Year Award. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Emile Hirsch to Star in Texas-Set Thriller 'The Violet Crown' (EXCLUSIVE)

A two-time Grammy and 13-time Latin Grammy Award-winning artist and producer, Rosalía is currently riding the success of her "LUX" album, released in 2025, which earned five Billboard No. 1 chart placements, entered the Billboard 200 at No. 4 and is nominated for nine 2027 Grammy Awards. Numerous outlets all named it among the year's best albums, and it has since picked up seven Latin Grammy nominations, while "La Perla" is nominated for best Latin song at the MTV Video Music Awards. Her earlier work laid the groundwork for that momentum: in 2022, she wrote, performed, recorded, and produced "Motomami," which debuted at No. 1 on Spotify's Global Album Chart, earned the year's highest Metacritic score, and fueled the sold-out Motomami World Tour. Before that, her breakthrough sophomore album, "El Mal Querer," reimagined flamenco for a new era and won a Grammy and eight Latin Grammys, including album of the year, while also making her the first Spanish-language artist nominated for best new artist at the Grammys. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Hilary Duff made a triumphant return to music this year with "luck… or something," her sixth studio album and first in a decade, via Atlantic Records. Co-written by Duff and produced by her husband, Grammy-winning songwriter and producer Matthew Koma, alongside Brian Phillips, the confessional pop record explores motherhood, marriage, and self-discovery in her 30s, led by singles "Mature," "Roommates," and "Weather for Tennis." The album debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200—marking her highest chart debut since 2007 and her sixth career Top 5 entry—while hitting No. 1 in Canada and Australia and earning "Best Albums of 2026" honors from Variety, Billboard, and Rolling Stone. A multiplatinum artist and 2026 TIME 100 honoree, Duff has also built a multifaceted career as an acclaimed actor (including an award-nominated role on "Younger"), producer, entrepreneur, philanthropist, and New York Times best-selling author. Following the surprise release of her re-recorded hits EP "(Mine)" and her new "Holiday Things" EP, Duff is currently in the middle of her sold-out global headline run, the lucky me tour—recently named Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year by Billboard — which has already expanded into 2027.

While her early releases established a devoted cult following, Slayyyter's "WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA" marked her boldest reinvention yet. Her third studio album is authentically her. The 4x Grammy nominee revisited her upbringing in St. Louis, and decided to make "iPod music" — a free-for-all of feral punk, corroded pop, and raunchy rap — conjuring the "Midwest-core tweaker bar rat" characters of her youth. Early singles "BEAT UP CHANEL$," "CANNIBALISM!,” and “CRANK ” steadily built hype for the project ahead of its release, with fans fervently embracing the raw, swaggering SLAYYYTER that emerged from the ashes of her past selves. articles.title: 5 Underseen Patrick Stewart Performances That Prove He Was One of the Best Actors Ever
articles.summary: Following the death of Sir Patrick Stewart, audiences are revisiting the career of one of the most prolific performers of his generation. The English actor's most famous portrayals include Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. Stewart’s legacy and reputation come from years of commanding, […]
articles.content:
Many of Stewart's most interesting performances have actually come from smaller productions, supporting roles, or titles the masses have simply forgotten. It’s true that these didn't receive the same attention as Picard or Xavier, but they reveal the staggering breadth of his acting cops, beyond a benevolent authority figure. Here are five stellar Patrick Stewart performances that remain criminally underseen.

In Christopher Ashley’s adaptation of Paul Rudnick’s Off-Broadway play, Patrick Stewart plays Sterling, a sophisticated Manhattan interior designer. The titular character Jeffrey, played by Steven Weber, is a gay New Yorker so frightened of contracting HIV that he decides to give up sex. Thus, when he falls for Steve (Stephen Geoffrey), who is HIV-positive, he’s forced to reconsider his celibacy. While Stweart’s character Sterling is not HIV-positive, his partner, Darius (Bryan Batt), is living with AIDS. Stewart brings levity to the film with his incredible comic timing and flamboyant wit, but the role also demands emotional authenticity as it portrays loving someone during the AIDS crisis. Many critics credited Stewart as one of the film’s greatest strengths. While Roger Ebert didn’t love the film as a whole due to its episodic feel, he singled out Stewart's Sterling as its “most sharply drawn and entertaining character,” praising his “barbed tongue” and “quick intelligence.”

In 1976, the BBC miniseries I, Claudius adapted Robert Graves’s novels about the Julio-Claudian emperors of Rome. Stewart appears in four of its 12 episodes as Lucius Aelius Sejanus, commander of the Praetorian Guard under Tiberius. As the emperor withdraws from public life, Sejanus grows his influence and tries to secure his position through marriage. Stewart plays the commander as an ambitious political operator whose discipline conceals an appetite for power. Predating the principled authority of Star Trek’s Jean-Luc Picard , Stewart utilizes a similar measured delivery and command, but in this case it’s a thin veneer over the character's calculating self-interest. It’s a small role that fans still remember well, and although the series was a British TV hit, it remains underseen in the US. With a fantastic ensemble that also includes Derek Jacobi, Siân Phillips, Brian Blessed, and John Hurt, I, Claudius is well worth a watch today.

The adult animated series American Dad! originally aired on Fox in 2005. Created by Seth MacFarlane, the irreverent sitcom follows a CIA agent named Stan Smith and his bizarro family. In the only voice performance on the list, Stewart portrays Avery Bullock, the CIA’s deputy director, and a recurring character throughout the show’s long run. Bullock is self-absorbed, sexually inappropriate, frequently intoxicated, and often cruel, yet Stewart performs him with all the polished diction and formal authority of a Shakespearean stage actor. Therein lies the comedic brilliance of the performance. By juxtaposing his British formality with the vulgar, absurd dialogue, Stewart (and MacFarlane) created a standout characte r in a series full of insane comedy gags. In an interview with TIME , Stewart expressed his endless enthusiasm for the role, saying that Bullock “Opened up opportunities for me I hadn’t had before. Playing an obnoxious, loud, opinionated, vulgar-minded, self-obsessed character was just fantastic.”

Safe House , directed by Eric Steven Stahl in 1998, is an underseen film in which Stewart gives one of his most raw and vulnerable performances. He plays Mace Sowell, a retired Defense Intelligence operative who believes a former boss is plotting his murder. Mace has also been diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer’s disease, leaving his daughter and others unsure whether his suspicions are founded or just symptoms of his declining condition. He fortifies his home with surveillance equipment and security systems. Both the film and Stewart's performance do a great job of sustaining the uncertainty and tension surrounding Mace’s paranoia. In many ways, Mace remains intelligent and capable, but even his confidence in his own judgment begins to fail him. In a Los Angeles Times review, Daryl H. Miller praised Stewart's portrayal of Mace's deteriorating independence, writing that there was something “terrifyingly believable” about his insistence that he had served in a secret assassination squad and was now being targeted to keep its history buried.

Jeremy Saulnier’s Green Room is about a punk band that witnesses a murder at an Oregon club run by white supremacists. The musicians become trapped backstage as the club’s owner, Darcy Banker, becomes determined to eliminate them. It’s Stewart who plays Darcy, in a significant departure from the typical good-natured on-screen persona he’d become associated with. Yet rather than portraying Darcy as a volatile extremist, Stewart’s Darcy is courteous and methodical, often discussing violence with nonchalance. While Stewart is in rare form as a manipulative psychopath, he still manages to stay true to his acting style by avoiding cartoonish villainy. A criminally underseen early A24 release, Green Room is a masterpiece in which Patrick Stewart gives the most unique and subversive performance of his impressive career.

articles.title: I Rewatched SNL’s Sister Sketch, And Caught A Few Funny Details
articles.summary: Little things that say a lot.
articles.content:
I can't remember the last time a Saturday Night Live sketch had people talking quite as much as the "Sister" sketch has . Former SNL writer and frequent host John Mulaney returned to host SNL this past weekend, and among the sketches featured was a faux medical ad for "Sister," the ultimate elder care provider for your family. The clip has sparked quite a bit of conversation after humorously raising the topic of daughters -- and in many cases, by proxy, their spouses -- being relied on more often than sons to make themselves available, and oftentimes upend their lives, to care for an aging parent. It's the rare kind of sketch that makes people laugh as much as it makes many want to cry at the truth of it.

One subtle detail that I appreciated was the fact that when Mulaney's "Brother" character texts his sister to alert her that "dad fell," we see that the previous text exchanges between the two siblings are bland Happy Birthday messages from brother .

At the very end of the sketch, I had to pause it to read the captions. As is the case in many pharmaceutical ads, this one wraps up with a nod to the company responsible for the treatment, and then runs through a rapid but alarming list of potential side effects.

This seems like a dry dig at "Brother," lest he forget that the person or people in need of care are presumably the same person/people who brought him into the world and raised him.

It seems fair to warn users that the sister who's being relied on to shoulder most or all of the responsibility of care might occasionally emotionally collapse under the weight of it. And it's also fair to warn users that this "elder care system" won't work on any sister who has the psychological support to help her see through any suggestion or pressure that she should be the sole person responsible for care-giving. Quantities are limited sounds more like a mention for an HSN sale item than it does for medical treatment, but I suppose the messaging really is true for all siblings. I sure am grateful for mine!

articles.content:
Much like the Battle of Gods arc before it, the Resurrection F arc originally began as a Dragon Ball Z feature film release before eventually being re-adapted into a TV version of the arc for the Dragon Ball Super TV anime series. But unlike the Battle of Gods arc, this arc remains divisive among fans to this day not because of its animation but with many of the choices it made at its core. This new remake does offer a chance to correct some of those past mistakes.

#DBSuperBeerus RoF: Episode 7 Trailer! pic.twitter.com/Ug7jcYZXS7

The post-credits scene for Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 6 sees a few members of the Frieza Force noting how they are trying to strengthen up their forces once more for the Emperor's return. It's a tease that fans would immediately recognize from the Resurrection F arc, and that's further confirmed to be the case as “Resurrection F” is the title of the next major episode. This raises a bunch of questions for the remake's take on the arc as the first two attempts have really divided fans over whether or not it was ultimately a successful return for Frieza in general .

The Resurrection F arc sees Frieza coming back to life, and achieving the godly level Golden Frieza form for the occasion. It's notable because it also features the debut of the Super Saiyan God Super Saiyan form, but was derided by fans for some of the decisions it made surrounding Gohan and Earth's other Z Fighters at the time. But a retooled version of the arc could improve it with this new remake series. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been dividing fans with its own changes seen thus far , but this will be the real test of the remake idea.

It's yet to be revealed how many episodes the Resurrection F arc will last within Dragon Ball Super: Beerus . With the Battle of Gods arc being condensed into just six episodes compared to the original version's 18, it's likely that this arc will be even shorter than that. It was only nine episodes long in the original anime, so a condensed and more streamlined version of the arc will work its way through in a much quicker fashion. Especially because there's still one more arc confirmed to be on the way .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has also confirmed it will be showcasing a new version of the Universe 6 arc after this, but has yet to confirm its total number of episodes. The anime is quickly approaching the end of the Fall 2026 slate, but it's likely that the series will be going beyond that into the Winter 2027 months beginning in January if each arc will have at least five to six episodes each. articles.title: The JSA May Be DC's First Team, But It's Secret Origin Changed Comics Forever
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics The Justice Society of America was the first superhero team, first coming together in All-Star Comics #3, released on November 22, 1940, just two years after Superman solidified the genre as a whole. The JSA would go on to define the Golden Age of heroism, and now stand as the grandfathers of DC's superhero community, […]
articles.content:
However, as much as the JSA contributed to the idea of superheroes working together in groups , it also opened a door that nobody acknowledges, but was just as important in the long run. The formation of the JSA marked the first inter-company crossover, as the characters actually came from two of the parent companies that would go on to one day form DC Comics. The JSA didn't just establish that superheroes could work together across books, but that heroes could bridge company-wide chasms to fight crime together, and it's them we have to thank for the golden age of crossovers we now live in.

Back in the earliest days of superhero comic books, publishing houses were a lot smaller and much more numerous. Two of the biggest names in the industry were National Allied Publications and All-American Publications, which were leaps and bounds ahead of the competition. National Allied controlled the heaviest hitter in the game, Superman, and many other smaller heroes such as the Spectre, Doctor Fate, and the Sandman. All-American, meanwhile, had the original Flash, Green Lantern, Atom, Hawkman , and even Wonder Woman under its belt. Together, these are some of DC's most foundational characters, but way back in the earliest days of the 1940s, they actually didn't even exist in the same world.

Or, at least, they didn't until All-Star Comics #3, which united many of these characters together in one super-team. This set a precedent not just for heroes coming together, but for companies working together to build one bigger universe, which would become a staple of the next several decades as DC Comics formed and grew, drawing other publishers under its umbrella. It established that the superhero world could always expand to include new members, priming fans to not just accept, but yearn for heroes from across the publishing pond to hop in and join in saving the day. From Captain Marvel to Captain Atom and Blue Beetle, tons of iconic DC heroes didn't actually start in DC Comics. The JSA set the trend for these heroes joining teams to establish themselves as part of the universe, which most of the biggest names would go on to do, but that's just looking at the heroes who stayed with DC permanently.

While many publishing houses rose and fell, the Big Two of DC and Marvel have long stood the test of time, folding others into them as they all but monopolized commercialized superherodom. They have often been painted as rivals, but that interpretation emerged mainly from fans until the early 2000s. Most of each company's employees have worked at the other at one point or another, with generations of creatives forming the backbone of these different but similar universes. It was only natural that these companies would cross over. The first team-up across universes came about in Superman vs. The Amazing Spider-Man: The Battle of the Century , which released on January 2, 1976. It sparked a whole wave of other crossovers between the Big Two, creating fan-favorites and classics like JLA/Avengers and the Amalgam Universe.

However, the mid 2000s saw an end to this phenomenon and cooperation, with executives like Dan DiDio pushing the idea of a rivalry to draw lines in fans and cultivate a competitive following. The companies wouldn't unite again until DiDio left DC, a twenty-one-year drought finally broken by Deadpool/Batman . Ever since, DC and Marvel have seen fit to publish even more crossovers, opening the doors to an infinite array of possibilities of seeing our favorite heroes fight crime together. We live in a renaissance of superhero crossovers, but it couldn't have started at all without the JSA opening the doors. They defined what superheroes should look like on a massive scale, and they deserve all the credit they get and so much more.

articles.title: Elon Musk Was Disappointed In His SNL Impression. Jeremy Culhane Dropped A Six-Word Response
articles.summary: The comic spoke out after Musk shared his thoughts.
articles.content:
The newest Saturday Night Live episode aired last weekend, with comedian John Mulaney serving as Season 52’s latest host and Phoebe Bridgers performing as the musical guest. Unsurprisingly, the episode began with a cold open centered around recent events, and it centered on the controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. As part of that segment, Elon Musk was lampooned by the show again and, after he expressed disappointment with the impression, cast member Jeremy Culhane reacted.

SNL ’s latest cold open sees the CIA gathering the U.S’ biggest tech magnates for a training session on not exposing secrets to potential operatives. The presiding official (played by Mulaney) speaks to Musk (Jeremy Culhane), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline) and Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson). After Mulaney’s character unsuccessfully tries to make his case, Huang ( played by returning cast member Bowen Yang ) warns his colleagues using his own experience.

Ultimately, the real Elon Musk appeared to be less than impressed with the sketch, in which Mulaney’s character used venn diagrams to explain to the CEOs that a woman wouldn’t truly be interested in them without an ulterior motive. In response, Musk dropped a comment under the sketch on X and included a diagram of his own:

Throughout the sketch, Culhane’s Musk makes several random statements at the fictional briefing, one of which sees him compare himself to James Bond and another in which he tries to connect with Huang over their leather jackets. It’s because of those random asides that both the CIA official and even Huang use spray bottles on Culhane’s Musk. On X , after someone ranked the performances the actual SpaceX founder shared his take on Culhane’s impression, writing:

This isn’t the first time Musk has taken issue with an impression of himself on Saturday Night Live . Back in late 2024, the tech mogul – who also hosted SNL in 2021 – called out Dana Carvey for his take on him. The following year would also see Musk chastise Mike Meyers’ impression of him as well. The Tesla figurehead is far from the only star to ever take issue with an impression, as Kanye West disliked Chris Redd’s impressio n of him Also, Ice Cube was dismissive of Kenan Thompson’s take on him.

After this latest Musk impression, Jeremy Culhane took to his Instagram story to share a headline about Musk’s reaction. The Sex Lives of College Girls alum simply added the following caption to his post:

Reading between the lines, Culhane’s response seems to be a bit of trolling on his part. He may not have gone into detail, but it’s easy to get the feeling that he’s not too perturbed by Musk’s reaction to his performance. On the night of the taping, the actor’s performance also generated considerable laughs from the live studio audience. As for whether Musk might feel compelled to issue a response to the comedian’s social media post, that remains to be seen.

articles.title: Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support
articles.summary: The Cannes Film Festival has condemned the latest prison sentence handed down to Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi, who won last year's Palme d’Or with “It Was Just an Accident,” and has called on the international community to rally forces to prevent his incarceration. Panahi has been sentenced by a Tehran Revolutionary Court to five years […]
articles.content:
The Cannes Film Festival has condemned the latest prison sentence handed down to Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi , who won last year's Palme d'Or with " It Was Just an Accident ," and has called on the international community to rally forces to prevent his incarceration.

Panahi has been sentenced by a Tehran Revolutionary Court to five years and one month in prison, along with the confiscation of his passport, a two-year travel ban and a two-year ban on using social media. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Emile Hirsch to Star in Texas-Set Thriller 'The Violet Crown' (EXCLUSIVE)

The filmmaker was already facing a one-year prison sentence and a two-year travel ban stemming from a separate ruling in 2025. A third legal case related to his filmmaking activities is also pending.

"The Cannes Film Festival firmly condemns the judicial persecution of Jafar Panahi and calls for the lifting of all sanctions that prevent him from traveling, creating and expressing himself freely," the festival said in a statement on Thursday.

"Alongside artists, festivals and cultural institutions around the world, the Cannes Film Festival calls on the international community to mobilize and make its collective voice heard in order to prevent his incarceration," the statement continued.

Panahi, who has repeatedly clashed with Iranian authorities over the past two decades, has continued making films despite being arrested, imprisoned and banned from working and traveling.

In 2010, he was banned from making movies, speaking to the press and traveling, but continued to make films clandestinely. He was arrested again in 2022 and released about seven months later. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Despite the risks of further imprisonment, Panahi has refused to leave Iran permanently and returned to his home country in March 2026 after traveling internationally, notably in the U.S., to promote "It Was Just an Accident," one of his most politically minded films to date.

"Arrested and imprisoned on several occasions simply for being a filmmaker, Jafar Panahi continues to pursue his work despite the painful conditions imposed upon him," Cannes said. "Loyal to his country and to his crews, he has always refused to go into exile, believing that he must remain in Iran and continue to work freely."

The festival, which is headed by Iris Knobloch and Thierry Fremaux, said the Palme d'Or recognized "a career dedicated to defending freedom of creation and expression."

"His freedom does not concern just one filmmaker: it concerns the right of all artists to think, create and express themselves without fearing imprisonment," Cannes said.

"Everyone knows it, and everyone stands behind it: ‘No artist should be imprisoned for their work, their ideas or their expression, in Iran or anywhere else.'"

Panahi has a long history with Cannes, dating back to 1995 when "The White Balloon" won the Caméra d'Or for best first film. His "Crimson Gold" won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize in 2003, while "Three Faces" competed for the Palme d'Or in 2018 and won the screenplay prize.

In 2010, Panahi was invited to serve on the Cannes jury while imprisoned in Iran. His chair was left empty during the opening ceremony in a symbolic gesture of support. Fifteen years later, he returned to the festival to receive the Palme d'Or for "It Was Just an Accident," a drama inspired by his experiences in prison.

Panahi previously told Variety that he was determined to remain in Iran despite the threat of imprisonment.

"I am the kind of person who needs to be in his country," Panahi said. "I need to breathe there and work there. And even if they want to go ahead with that prison sentence, they can go ahead. Nothing will change my mind about going back."

articles.title: The "5,000 Episodes a Week" AI-Podcast Company Has Pivoted
articles.summary: After creating more than 15,000 AI-generated podcasts, causing strong reactions in the industry, former Wondery exec Jeanine Wright's Inception AI has rebranded into a B2B firm focused on video podcasting.
articles.content:
After launching a podcast network last fall with thousands of AI-generated podcasts and AI -podcast hosts, Inception AI has pivoted.

Over the last few months, the company has stopped work on its owned and operated podcasts, which numbered more than 15,000 and ignited strong reactions in the industry, essentially letting them fall dormant and no longer monetizing the shows. The company has instead moved into liquid content, helping other companies translate text to audio and create podcast videos from audio content, and rebranded under the name Liquid Studios, with another bold claim.

"I think we've solved podcast video," CEO Jeanine Wright tells The Hollywood Reporter of the new plan.

The decision to pivot came in mid-July, as both a bet on growth and in response to uneasiness about AI in the marketplace. The launch of their content offerings had made a splash and invoked a degree of vitriol, with Wright noting that she had been boo'd while taking the stage at podcast conferences, though she said she would later be pulled aside for business inquiries. The original vision for the company was to create content and provide services to other businesses, but the company ran into headwinds on the content side, which at one point included producing more than 3,000 episodes a week and creating more than 50 AI personalities to host content produced for $1 an episode or less.

The thousands of shows had been monetized through programmatic advertising, but the team ran into an issue when some of the marketplaces were unable to clearly identify to advertisers which shows were made with AI. The episodes included the AI-disclaimer in the audio and episode notes.

"We started to get some feedback from our programmatic partners that their customers wanted to know when they were advertising in something that was AI, and that they hadn't built out the infrastructure yet to be able to clearly identify to them when they were advertising in something with AI, and how it was performing," Wright said. She added that she mulled switching to direct sales instead, but that would've required more work from the small team.

Additionally, Wright had heard concerns about information contained in some of the episodes of the company's back-catalog of more than 350,000 episodes. Pre-pivot, some of the AI-created podcast hosts had operated in the health and wellness field, and referred to themselves as doctors or mental health professionals.

While Wright said the AI-made creators did not give medical advice – they offered home remedies for a cold or provided information on what depression and anxiety are – the concerns about representation were enough to cause the company to stop releasing new episodes from those creators in the winter. The team then went through and took down all related episodes from the back catalog. But that experience, as well as prior concerns they had received about the quality of past show episodes and show art, which were created with older versions of AI models, made Wright realize how much work would be required to maintain all of the back catalog, both editorially and as AI models evolve.

"It opened the question and the conversation of how are we going to look at our obligations and our responsibilities with respect to maintaining, updating what was this huge body of content that we had created in the past," Wright said.

The company had closed a $5 million seed round led by venture capital firm Activate Venture Partners in January, and in keeping with its commitments to investors pivoted to B2B as a better growth strategy. With the pivot, and using AI to help translate human-led projects into other mediums, Wright added that the industry has also been more receptive.

"I thought that within a year, people wouldn't care whether or not something was materially made with AI. I think people still care. I think I was wrong," Wright said.

The formerly eight-person company has now grown to 11. But, after moving away from making their own content, the company lost two of its co-founders, lifestyle guru and former television host Katie Brown, who previously led the content team, and her husband, William Corbin, who was chief technology officer of the company.

As it stands, Liquid Studios has about a dozen customers who are expected to go public this month, Wright said, and about a dozen more that are confidential, with clients including media companies, publishing houses, and large independent creators, brands and one company with a large television archive, with much of the current focus around turning audio into video, as well as text to audio and translation into other languages. The company went public in October and recently launched a pilot program to turn industry news podcast audio from PodNews into video.

To translate audio to video and more, Liquid Studios is using AI orchestration, which selects and coordinates the best AI models, video generators and more to use for the project. Related images and animation are pulled to create the videos, in styles ranging from animated to realistic, and clients can decide whether to use AI-generated images or not. The company also has the ability to create photorealistic or animated digital replicas of the podcast hosts to appear in the videos, cloning both the actual host's voice and look, but U.S.-based clients have been nervous to take it public because of how the market will react

"In the [user-generated content] space, I think we're seeing it a lot. But in the traditional creator space, I think it's coming, but it's not here yet," Wright said.

Wright says she believes the company's new model helps creators approach the increasingly visual medium of podcasting and help them visualize content without the costs associated with a larger production studio. As it stands, the company is going to market with a rate of $10 a finished minute of audio to video conversion.

Photo credit: Paramount+ Avatar: Seven Havens is currently taking up all of the attention right now, but the co-creator behind the franchise has addressed when fans might be able to see the next major series coming in the Avatar Studios pipeline. And it's going to take a lot longer than what fans might think. Avatar Studios kicked off […]
articles.content:
Konietzko and DiMartino announced during New York Comic Con 2026 earlier this Fall that Avatar Studios is already hard at work on the next major series, Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos . This new series will be going back in time with the Avatar Cycle to focus on the titular Kuruk's time as the Avatar, and when asked about its potential release window by IGN , DiMartino revealed that it's entirely up to Paramount but also reveals that it might be a while before we see the series as “That's just getting started.”

“That is beyond my scope of control, DiMartino stated when asked about when Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos could potentially release. “So it'll depend on what Paramount Plus wants to do, I guess, or whatever the streaming app happens to be at that time.” But it also turns out that it might be much further off than fans would hope for as DiMartino elaborates with, “That's just getting started. It might be a bit before we have episodes ready for that.” But with so little revealed about this new series thus far , waiting a bit longer for its release makes a lot of sense.

Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos will feature Bryan Konietzko and Michael DiMartino as showrunners for the series produced in collaboration with Avatar Studios and Nickelodeon Animation Studios for a release with Paramount+ . No release window had been announced for the series when it was first announced, and DiMartino's comments tease that its release is likely further away. But it's likely going to release sometime after Avatar: Seven Havens ends its own run. And that's going to be sooner than you think as well.

Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 has been confirmed to make its debut with Paramount+ next May, and then Season 3 of the series will follow later in 2027. With two seasons coming next year, and a confirmation that it will end with its fourth season , this opens up a space for Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos to release shortly after. If we're lucky, the new series could be making its debut sometime in late 2028 right after Avatar: Seven Havens wraps up its four season run. This would keep the hype train rolling along for sure.

When choosing to focus on Kuruk's story for its own series, DiMartino told ComicBook that the initiative with Avatar Studios was to develop new projects that felt different from one another in style and genre, “When Brian [Konietzko] and I came to start Avatar Studios, since we were developing multiple things at once, we were very conscious of making sure each project felt different in genre and tone style and everything.” This teases an entirely different kind of series than seen before, so what are you hoping to see from the new Avatar Kuruk series? Let us know all of your thoughts in the comments.
